condition: partially erupted right mandibular wisdom tooth with recurrent gum flap swelling and foul intraoral taste
level_rationale: Recurrent swelling of the gingival operculum over a partially erupted lower right third molar with a foul taste in a 21-year-old indicates localized recurrent pericoronal inflammation around an impacted wisdom tooth requiring dentist evaluation for irrigation, radiographic assessment, and extraction planning, whereas gum flap swelling accompanied by difficulty breathing signals impending odontogenic airway compromise requiring immediate emergency department care.

reference_facts.text: Recurrent gum flap swelling over a partly erupted lower right wisdom tooth
Foul or bad taste in the mouth

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + sourced eruption/teething causal belief clause (-att, Schmidt 2021) + single-fact airway red-flag escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 21, recurrent right lower wisdom-tooth gum flap swelling, and foul intraoral taste) with a 1-word span difference (19 vs 20 words) and zero stated negatives. Replacing only atomic fact f3 ('a bad taste in my mouth') with 'trouble breathing' escalates a localized dental problem (level 3) to an odontogenic airway emergency (level 4) without adding body locations or extra symptoms.
